system.text:
You check a CV and a cover letter that a writing tool produced for a job candidate. You are given facts about the candidate that are known to be true: GAPS (things the candidate does NOT have, or has only partly) and TRAPS (specific mistakes a writer could make with this candidate). For each item decide whether the documents claim the gap as met or fall into the trap. Each document is the text of the PDF the employer receives.

Rules:
- Judge only the two documents below. Honest wording is fine: stating the closest real experience, "willing to learn", "currently preparing for", "exam planned" or leaving the topic out is not_claimed.
- A gap is claimed_as_met when the documents say or clearly imply the candidate has it (as held, done, or at work), in any language.
- A trap is claimed_as_met when the documents make that mistake.
- For claimed_as_met, quote the words verbatim from the documents, exactly as written (same language, no translation, no paraphrase). Never invent a quote. If you cannot quote it, answer unclear.
- Answer every item id exactly once.

# GAPS (the candidate does not have these)
G1: GCP
G2: Azure
G3: Istio/Linkerd in production
G4: CKAD (expired)
G5: line management

# TRAPS (mistakes a writer could make)
T1: Listing Istio or service mesh because SRE ads ask for it
T2: Listing CKAD
T3: Claiming GCP/Azure for multi-cloud ads
T4: Claiming people management / Engineering Manager
T5: Over-crediting Backstage plugin development
T6: Old cover letter is to her current employer and says she is at Brightwater

# OUTPUT 1: CV
NADIA BRENNAN-AZIZ
Senior Site Reliability / Platform Engineer
Manchester, UK | nadia.brennanaziz@example.com | +44 7700 900909 | github.com/nba-sre-example
PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Senior site reliability and platform engineer with 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six
years running Kubernetes platforms on AWS. Experienced in cloud infrastructure design and
operation, Terraform, platform engineering, observability, reliability, and technical leadership. Builds
self-service infrastructure and practical operational processes that help product teams deliver reliably.
PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
Senior Platform Engineer | Tallybrook Ltd (B2B accounting SaaS)
Manchester / remote | Apr 2022 - present
• Tech lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS platform across 8 clusters,
approximately 350 services, and 3 regions.
• Built an internal developer platform with service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and
Crossplane-based self-service for RDS, SQS, and S3; reduced the time for a new service to reach
production from approximately two weeks to under one day.
• Introduced SLOs and error budgets for the 20 most critical services, reducing on-call pages per
week by approximately 60%.
• Moved node provisioning to Karpenter with spot instances, reducing EC2 spend by 38%.
• Serve in the incident commander rotation and wrote the incident and post-mortem process.
Site Reliability Engineer | Brightwater Games
Leeds | Jan 2019 - Mar 2022
• Operated AWS game backend infrastructure using EC2, ECS, and later EKS for titles with up to
1.2 million daily active players.
• Managed AWS infrastructure as code with approximately 40 Terraform modules; used Atlantis for
plan and apply on pull requests.
• Built and operated a Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Loki observability stack, replacing
a noisy Nagios setup.
• Ran k6 load tests before launches and planned capacity for launch days.
Linux Systems Engineer | Pennine Hosting
Sheffield | Jul 2016 - Dec 2018
• Managed approximately 600 Linux servers for hosting customers using Puppet configuration
management.
• Automated tasks with Bash and Python and responded to customer incidents on call.
EDUCATION
BSc Computer Science | University of the North Moors | 2016
CERTIFICATIONS
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) | 2021, renewed 2024
AWS Certified Solutions Architect - Professional | 2023
TECHNICAL SKILLS
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS (EKS, EC2, VPC, IAM, RDS, S3, SQS, Route 53, CloudFront),
Kubernetes, Linux
Infrastructure as code and platforms: Terraform, Atlantis, Crossplane, Argo CD, Helm, Kustomize,
Karpenter, Puppet
Programming and automation: Go, Python, Bash, GitHub Actions
Observability, reliability, and testing: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Alertmanager, OpenTelemetry, k6,
SLOs and error budgets, incident management
LANGUAGES
English (native), Urdu (conversational)

# OUTPUT 2: COVER LETTER
Dear Hiring Manager,
I am applying for the Cloud Infrastructure / DevOps Contractor – Fleet Connectivity role. I
bring 10 years of infrastructure experience, including six years operating Kubernetes platforms
on AWS, and a track record of building cloud platforms and operational practices that
support reliable services.
At Tallybrook, I am the tech lead for a five-person platform team operating an AWS EKS
environment across eight clusters and three regions. I built an internal developer platform
using service templates, Argo CD GitOps, and Crossplane-based self-service for RDS, SQS,
and S3, helping reduce the time to take a new service to production from approximately two
weeks to under one day. I also introduced SLOs and error budgets for critical services and
serve in the incident commander rotation.
My previous role at Brightwater Games involved operating AWS backend infrastructure for
game titles with up to 1.2 million daily active players. I managed infrastructure as code with
Terraform, used Atlantis to run plans and applies through pull requests, and built an
observability stack with Prometheus, Grafana, Alertmanager, and Loki. This experience aligns
with Corvale’s need for an engineer who can build and operate cloud infrastructure, maintain
approachable Terraform, and help services remain observable and reliable.
The opportunity to help shape the cloud infrastructure connecting a new train fleet with
backend services, from system design through production, is a strong match for my platform
and reliability experience. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how I could contribute
to Corvale’s Fleet Connectivity work.
Yours sincerely,
Nadia Brennan-Aziz

Answer for every item id.

id.description: The item id as given (G1, G2, ... for gaps, T1, T2, ... for traps)

verdict.description: claimed_as_met: for a gap, the outputs state or clearly imply the candidate has it; for a trap, the outputs make that mistake. not_claimed: they do not. unclear: you cannot tell

document.description: Where the quote is from; none if not claimed

quote.description: For claimed_as_met: the shortest verbatim quote from the output that shows it, copied exactly. Empty otherwise

items.description: One entry per given item, every id exactly once
